newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Alpi Eagles airline to resume flights.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Alpi Eagles airline to resume flights.

text.p: Italian private airline Alpi Eagles will be allowed to resume flying next week after its four Fokker 100 planes were grounded last week by the civil aviation authority, Milan business daily Il Sole 24 Ore reported.
No comment was immediately available from the air carrier.

Il Sole 24 Ore said three of the airline's planes will re-enter service on Monday on routes between Venice and Verona, in the north of the country, and Rome and a fourth plane is expected to start flying again the following day.
The new airline's fleet was grounded last week after civil aviation inspectors found irregularities in the way flight records were being logged.
Following the grounding Alpi Eagles sacked ithe chief pilot, the director of operations and the head of technical maintenance and drew up a program to tighten safety precautions.
